analysis:
Examined the base text (lines 1047-1611) and head text (lines 1-551) of ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift. The changes visible in the patch excerpt are refactors of load-admission memory arithmetic: reclaimableMemoryGb and reclaimableMemoryBytes gain a countingRetainedKVSegments parameter, a new evictionCanReach helper is added, and the comments on admission and throwIfRetiring change. The head ranges for those changes (about lines 1305-1589) are beyond the supplied head text, which stops at line 551, so the new eviction and reclaim logic was reviewed only through the truncated patch excerpt and the base. Per that excerpt, the change affects only whether a model load is admitted or evicted under memory pressure. That is an availability and capacity concern (T-010, T-029) and touches no consumer plaintext, key custody, attestation or authorization paths.

The head text I could read (lines 1-551) is the weight-hash capture and publish flow. It contains the fresh-cryptographic-hash requirement for reusable SSD loads, the pre/post-load hash comparison in finalizeReusableSSDLoad, and markWeightHashUnavailable, which fails closed by disabling the SSD cache and clearing the stale hash. This is consistent with the T-041 mitigations (verified weightHash binding) and the T-012/T-027 weight-substitution concerns. Whether those lines are changed in this PR is not shown. I found no regression.

Remaining questions for integration: (1) The head implementation of the new reclaim and evictionCanReach code, and the truncated patch tail (credit for retained KV segments), were not fully visible. Over-crediting reclaimable memory could admit loads that then fail with a 503, an availability issue only. (2) The pre/post-load hash logic after head line 551 was not visible.
